title: Partner Ecosystems Earned Their Strategic Seat At The Table — Now What?
summary: B2B partner leaders have worked to prove that ecosystems deserve strategic attention. Our latest data suggests that this battle has already been won.
body_markdown:
## **Partner Ecosystem Strategy Is Business Strategy**


For years, B2B partner ecosystem leaders have worked to prove that partner ecosystems deserve strategic attention. Our latest survey data suggests that this battle has largely been won. According to[The State Of B2B Partner Ecosystems, 2026](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-state-of-b2b-partner-ecosystems-2026/RES202815) , 70% of partner ecosystem and channel marketing decision-makers say that orchestrating or optimizing a partner ecosystem is very important or absolutely essential to their organization.


## **The Business Impact Is Difficult To Ignore**


Why the heightened attention? The growing importance of partner ecosystems is not simply a matter of executive perception. It is grounded in measurable business impact. Nearly 60% of respondents to our survey reported that over 40% of their organization’s revenue is attributable to partners and indirect routes to market. This finding also underscores a significant shift in how organizations create value. Partner ecosystems are not merely generating resell transactions.


Our research reveals that partner ecosystems are going further by helping B2B providers drive innovation, extend their offering portfolios, expand market reach, support buyers throughout increasingly complex purchasing journeys, provide specialized expertise, and contribute to revenue outcomes in ways that extend beyond traditional channel models. As partner ecosystems expand and mature, their influence increasingly spans both indirect and direct revenue opportunities. But despite the now widespread recognition of the importance and value of partner ecosystems, a critical gap remains.


## **The Greatest Risk Is Underinvestment**


When asked about the biggest barriers to partner ecosystem success, 50% of respondents identified a lack of resources as a top challenge. While supplier organizations increasingly understand the value of partner ecosystems, many have yet to make the investments necessary to fully capitalize on them.


The implications are significant. As buyers increasingly evaluate the strength of a provider’s ecosystem alongside its products and services, expanded investment in the people, leadership, and capabilities to orchestrate partner ecosystems effectively will drive greater growth and create differentiated customer value. The question is no longer whether partner ecosystems matter but whether organizations are investing in them at a level that matches their strategic importance.


## **Closing The Partner Ecosystem Investment Gap**


If your organization views partner ecosystems as essential to growth, innovation, revenue generation, customer value, and competitive differentiation, now is the time to assess whether your partner ecosystem investments align with those expectations. Evaluate the resources, skills, leadership, and operational support required for your partner ecosystem initiatives and identify gaps that could limit future success.


To learn more about expected partner ecosystem growth, revenue trends, and the challenges that supplier organizations must address to maximize value, read[The State Of B2B Partner Ecosystems, 2026](https://www.forrester.com/report/the-state-of-b2b-partner-ecosystems-2026/RES202815) and reach out to schedule aninquiry or guidance session .
